_comment: Turkish terms chosen for the social-thought-roots lesson. status: ok = attested in a Turkish source I opened; chosen = my own rendering of an English/German/French term (no Turkish source checked); check = weakly attested, needs a Turkish-language reviewer. See content/research-notes/social-thought-roots.md.

sociology.note: Used in the TDV and Türk Maarif entries on Gökalp. Older Turkish usage: ‘içtimaiyat’, ‘ilm-i içtimâ’ (both seen on those pages).

social-facts.note: The TDV entry on Gökalp uses ‘sosyal olgu’; ‘toplumsal olgu’ is my choice for consistency with ‘toplumsal’ elsewhere in the course.

treat-facts-as-things.en: treat social facts as things (traiter les faits sociaux comme des choses)
treat-facts-as-things.tr: toplumsal olguları şey gibi ele al
treat-facts-as-things.note: Gökalp’s ‘şey’î’ (objective) noted in the TDV entry; see the deep card.

mechanical-solidarity.note: The TDV entry says Gökalp adopted the transition ‘mekanik toplumdan organik topluma’; ‘dayanışma’ is my rendering of solidarité.

verstehen.note: ‘Anlayıcı/yorumlayıcı sosyoloji’ for verstehende Soziologie is my rendering; Turkish textbook usage not checked.

ideal-type.note: Used in the TÜBİTAK encyclopedia entry (Bulut).

legitimate-domination.note: Deliberately given as a pair; see the deep card. ‘Egemenlik’ usually means sovereignty in Turkish.

iron-cage.en: iron cage / shell as hard as steel (stahlhartes Gehäuse)
iron-cage.tr: demir kafes / çelik gibi sert kabuk
iron-cage.note: ‘Demir kafes’ not verified in Turkish sources; both renderings are given in the deep card.

gemeinschaft-gesellschaft.note: Both pairs are given in the TÜBİTAK entry (Bulut); the Turkish translation title is ‘Cemaat ve Cemiyet’ (Güler 2019).

wesenwille-kurwille.note: German terms kept in the text.

mobilization-of-bias.note: Our own translation of Lukes’s phrase; the English term is given at first mention.

culture-civilization-gokalp.en: culture and civilization (Gökalp’s hars and medeniyet)
culture-civilization-gokalp.note: Seen on the TDV and Türk Maarif pages on Gökalp.
